items.vault_note: vault/05 - Business Management/Problem Bank/Problem - Bank C24 - Radome Composites Accruals and Classification.md
items.statement_html: The owner of Radome Composites S.L., which makes radar domes for aircraft noses, says: "In December we delivered 20 domes to an airline that will pay in February, so they are not sales of this year. We received in November a 30,000 m.u. advance for domes to be delivered next March, so that is income of this year. The electricity of December will be paid in January, so it is a cost of next year. And the five-year bank loan is all a long-term debt, even the instalment due next June."

subquestions.label: a
subquestions.prompt_html: Correct the owner's four statements using the accrual principle and the classification of the balance sheet
subquestions.hint_html: Revenues are recorded when the sale is made, expenses when goods and services are received, whether paid or not [Slide 8]. Current items are settled within one year [Slides 14-16].
subquestions.checkpoint_html:
• December deliveries: revenue of this year; the amount owed is an account receivable (current asset).
  • November advance: not revenue yet; a liability (unearned revenue) until delivery in March.
  • December electricity: expense of this year; unpaid amount is a current liability.
  • Loan: the instalment due next June is a current liability; the rest is long-term.
subquestions.solution_html:
Owner's statementCorrectionBasis
December deliveries are not sales of this yearThey are revenue of this year: the sale was made in December. The amount owed is an account receivable, a current assetRevenues are recorded when the sale is made, paid or not [Slide 8]; current assets [Slide 14]
The November advance is income of this yearIt is not revenue yet: no domes have been delivered. It is a liability (unearned revenue) until MarchLiabilities include unearned revenues [Slide 13]
December electricity is a cost of next yearIt is an expense of this year: the service was received in December. The unpaid amount is a current liabilityExpenses are recorded when the services are received [Slide 8]
The whole loan is long-termThe instalment due next June is a current liability; only the instalments due after one year are long-termCurrent liabilities are paid within the coming year [Slide 16]

subquestions.label: b
subquestions.prompt_html: Explain why the income statement and the balance sheet need these rules
subquestions.hint_html: What does each statement report, and over what time [Slides 7, 12]?
subquestions.checkpoint_html:
• The income statement reports performance over a period: it must match the revenues and expenses of that period, not cash movements.
  • The balance sheet reports the financial position at a point in time: classifying by maturity shows liquidity.
subquestions.solution_html: The income statement reports the performance of the business over a specific period [Slide 7]: it must contain the revenues earned and the expenses incurred in that period, whatever happens to the cash, otherwise the profit of a year would depend on when customers happen to pay. The balance sheet reports the financial position at a particular point in time [Slide 12]: splitting assets and liabilities into current and non-current shows whether the company can meet the debts due within the year with the resources that become cash within the year.

items.statement_html:
The newly appointed financial director of LOGÍSTICA FRIGORÍFICA DEL LEVANTE S.L. (FRIGOLEV), a company located in the port area of Castellón and dedicated to the manufacturing of isothermal containers and cold-chain storage equipment for agricultural exporters, is working on the closing of its financial statements (balance sheet and Income Statement) as of 31 December 2018 (31/12/2018).

The company was originally incorporated on 1 January 2016 (01/01/2016) by four partners, with an initial contribution of each of 1.500 m.u. disbursed fully in cash at that time, and no further capital modifications took place until fiscal year 2018. Due to the sudden departure of the previous chief accountant, the financial director only has an incomplete balance of the company as of 31 December 2017 (31/12/2017), which is included below with certain missing figures marked as (?), along with the audit notes detailing the operations that have taken place during the period from 1 January 2018 (01/01/2018) to 31 December 2018 (31/12/2018):

I. On 31 December 2017 (31/12/2017), the company had as depreciable fixed assets only the industrial refrigeration chambers purchased on a certain date during 2016, which have a useful life of 10 years and are amortized linearly with a residual value of 10% of their acquisition cost. In addition, the balance sheet at 31 December 2017 (31/12/2017) reflected an industrial plot of land acquired in 2016 and financial shares of other companies acquired as a permanent investment.

II. During the year 2018, the company has sold 3.600 units of isothermal containers at a catalog price of 25 m.u. / unit (every month the same amount, 300 u.). The general payment condition agreed with the customers implies that this will occur 60 days after the sale. However, a very important agricultural cooperative (representing 25% of the physical units sold each month), which has bought an equal amount every month, has been given a discount of 8% on the catalog price of their purchases in exchange for paying strictly in cash in the same month of the sale.

III. At 31 December 2017 (31/12/2017) there was a stock (stock in stock) of 400 tons of insulating raw material valued at 2,00 m.u. / ton. On 1 April 2018 (01/04/2018), the company purchased 5.000 tons of raw material at a cost of 2,00 m.u. / ton. The payment condition agreed with the suppliers was 40% paid in cash on the date of purchase, 30% payable to 90 days, and the remaining 30% deferred until 1 February 2019 (01/02/2019). At 31 December 2018 (31/12/2018), after conducting the warehouse count, there remains a final stock (stock in stock) of 900 tons.

IV. During the first quarter of 2018, the unpaid taxes and the outstanding supplier balances from the previous year were paid in full. Regarding the customer debt outstanding from 31 December 2017 (31/12/2017), 75% was charged in cash during the first semester of 2018, except 200 m.u. from a customer who requested and was granted a deferral of payment until 15 March 2019 (15/03/2019), and 100 m.u. corresponding to a client declared definitively insolvent on 1 June 2018 (01/06/2018), which must be recorded as an unrecoverable bad debt loss for the period.

V. Fixed personnel expenses have been 2.200 m.u. / month (to which 600 m.u. / month must be added for Social Security) from 1 January 2018 (01/01/2018). To respond to seasonal peaks in container assembly, production staff also received variable wages that amounted in 2018 to 3.620 m.u. Fixed and variable wages are paid in the month in which they are produced, whereas Social Security contributions (starting from January 2018) are paid on the 15th day of the following month. General expenses and utilities (electricity, phone, insurance, etc.) amounted to 1.100 m.u. / month and are paid two months after being made.

VI. The company carried out a renting contract on 1 March 2018 (01/03/2018) (with a duration of 2 years) with a specialized company for electric warehouse forklifts, for a value of 350 m.u. monthly. The contract establishes a condition of payment to 90 days (payment at the end of each month).

VII. On 1 April 2018 (01/04/2018), the company made a capital increase by issuing 1.000 new shares of 2,00 m.u. nominal value each, fully disbursed in cash and with an issue premium of 50% over the nominal value. On the same date, 1 April 2018 (01/04/2018), it bought two refrigerated delivery vehicles that cost a total of 4.800 m.u., of which it paid 50% in cash, postponing the payment of the remainder in two equal installments: half on 1 October 2018 (01/10/2018) and the other half on 1 April 2019 (01/04/2019). These vehicles will be amortized linearly in 6 years with a total residual value of 480 m.u. Furthermore, on 1 October 2018 (01/10/2018), it bought a software license for cold-chain tracking for a value of 1.600 m.u., payable to 120 days, which is amortized linearly in 4 years with residual value zero.

VIII. The long-term bank loan appearing on the balance sheet at 31 December 2017 (31/12/2017) was granted on 1 January 2017 (01/01/2017) at an annual interest rate of 6%. Each 31 December, the company must pay the accrued annual interest calculated from the loan value at the beginning of each year, and starting on 31 December 2018 (31/12/2018) it must also return to the bank an annual principal amount of 500 m.u. until completing the repayment on 31 December 2021 (31/12/2021). Additionally, on 1 July 2018 (01/07/2018), the company obtained a new short-term bank credit of 1.500 m.u. at 8% annual interest, agreeing to return 50% of the principal each semester for the next year. Both the principal installment and the semiannual interest calculated on the amount actually due in that semester will be paid the day after the end of each semester (i.e., on 1 January 2019 (01/01/2019) and 1 July 2019 (01/07/2019)).

IX. The financial results of the company are declared at 23:59 hrs on 31 December 2018 (31/12/2018). The applicable corporation tax rate is 25% on the Profits obtained, which is settled by calendar year and will be paid to the Treasury on 20 January 2019 (20/01/2019) (counted in the balance at 31 December 2018 (31/12/2018) as "unpaid taxes"). From the net profit after taxes, the company first offsets in full the losses from previous years, and of the remaining net profit, it retains 60% as reserves and distributes the other 40% as dividends to the shareholders, which are paid in cash before carrying out the final balance at 24:00 on 31 December 2018 (31/12/2018).

Step 1. New sales of the cooperative

$$75 \times 0{,}90 = 67{,}5 \text{ u./month}, \qquad 67{,}5 \times 25 = 1.687{,}5 \text{ m.u./month}, \qquad 12 \times 1.687{,}5 = 20.250 \text{ m.u.}$$
$$\Delta\text{Revenue} = 20.250 - 20.700 = -450 \text{ m.u.} \;\Rightarrow\; \text{Revenue} = 87.750 \text{ m.u.}$$

Step 2. Raw material (hypothesis 4)

In the base case 4.500 tons were consumed for 3.600 units: $4.500 / 3.600 = 1{,}25$ t/unit $= 2{,}50$ m.u./unit. Selling $12 \times 7{,}5 = 90$ units fewer:

$$\Delta\text{Consumption} = -90 \times 2{,}50 = -225 \text{ m.u.} \;\Rightarrow\; \text{final stock} = 1.800 + 225 = 2.025 \text{ m.u.}$$

$$\text{Profit before taxes} = 24.000 - 450 + 225 = 23.775, \qquad \text{Tax} = 0{,}25 \times 23.775 = 5.943{,}75$$
$$\text{Net profit} = 23.775 - 5.943{,}75 = 17.831{,}25, \qquad \text{Remaining} = 17.431{,}25$$
$$\text{Reserves} = 0{,}60 \times 17.431{,}25 = 10.458{,}75, \qquad \text{Dividends} = 0{,}40 \times 17.431{,}25 = 6.972{,}50$$

Step 4. New cash

The cooperative now pays at 60 days: January to October collected, $10 \times 1.687{,}5 = 16.875$ instead of 20.700 (−3.825). The dividend paid falls by 67,50; the tax is not paid in 2018.

$$\text{Cash} = 14.060 - 3.825 + 67{,}50 = 10.302{,}50 \text{ m.u.}$$

The profit is higher with the discount (18.000 against 17.831,25): removing the discount gains $2$ m.u. on each of the 810 units the cooperative still buys ($810 \times 2 = 1.620$ m.u.), but the 90 units it stops buying carried a margin over raw material of $23 - 2{,}50 = 20{,}50$ m.u. each ($90 \times 20{,}50 = 1.845$ m.u.); the net effect before taxes is $1.620 - 1.845 = -225$ m.u. items.statement_html:
The company AGRODRON LEVANTE S.L. was incorporated on 1 January 2017 (01/01/2017) by a group of agricultural engineers with a registered paid-in capital of 4.500 m.u., having an objective of providing precision crop-monitoring services by drone and distributing organic fertilizers in the region of Murcia.

The following information applies to fiscal year 2017:

To finance the operations of the company, on 1 January 2017 (01/01/2017) a bank granted the company a loan of 1.500 m.u. at 6% annual interest, with a duration of 5 years, i.e. until 31 December 2021 (31/12/2021). Each 31 December, the company must return to the bank an equal principal amount of 300 m.u. and should also pay the due annual interest (6%) calculated from the loan value at the beginning of each year.

During 2017, the company invested in a fleet of agricultural drones worth 2.400 m.u. The useful life of the drones purchased was 8 years (amortized linearly, with no residual value) and at the end of 2017 the company recorded in accumulated depreciation an amount of 75 m.u. for those assets. Also, a further investment of 400 m.u. in mapping software licenses was made on 31 December 2017 (31/12/2017) to process aerial images. They use these licenses for 4 years (linear amortization with residual value zero). In addition, the company spent 800 m.u. to purchase a plot of rural land for its flight testing base. Most of 2017 was devoted to obtaining civil aviation permits and only the actual business work was started in the final months of the year. At 31 December 2017 (31/12/2017), its balance sheet reflected a loss of 220 m.u., there was no stock (stock in stock) nor pending customer or supplier balances, and the cash in hand and bank account was 1.955 m.u.

The following information applies to fiscal year 2018:

  • For aerial crop monitoring, the average number of subscribed farms during 2018 was 400 with an average revenue of 0,45 m.u. / month per client in subscription fees. Additionally, the company billed 840 m.u. for the direct sales of organic fertilizers. At the end of 2018, AGRODRON had accounts receivable of 310 m.u. from their customers.
  • The company purchased supplies of organic fertilizers during 2018 which amounted to 500 m.u. Of these purchases, 70% was paid immediately in cash and the payment of the remaining 30% was deferred to the following year. Year 2018 sales consumed 80% of the purchased goods.
  • AGRODRON operates from rented hangars that have a monthly cost (from 1 January 2018 (01/01/2018)) of 25 m.u. / month, paid in cash. Fixed salaries and Social Security costs (contribution of the company to the Social Security) of the permanent employees amounted to 60 m.u. per month (from 1 January 2018 (01/01/2018)) and were paid in full in 2018. To respond to increased demand during the harvest campaign, the company hired external pilots whose variable wages amounted in 2018 to 192 m.u. (paid in cash).
  • Electricity, insurance, and other administrative expenditures totaled 180 m.u. in 2018. The company postponed the payment of 40% of this amount to the following year. Furthermore, on 1 July 2018 (01/07/2018), the company acquired thermal cameras for its drones for a value of 200 m.u., paying 50% in cash on that date and leaving the remainder payable to 9 months, i.e. on 1 April 2019 (01/04/2019). This equipment has a useful life of 5 years and will be amortized linearly with a residual value of 20%.
  • The financial results of the company are declared at 23:59 hrs on 31 December 2018 (31/12/2018). The applicable corporation tax rate was 25% on the Profits obtained and is payable in the first quarter of 2019. In 2018, the results were positive: after offsetting in full the loss of the previous year, the company decided to distribute 30% of the remaining net profit after taxes as dividends (paid at 24:00 on 31 December 2018 (31/12/2018)) and retain the rest in the company.

Required:

  1. Construct the Income Statement (Profit and Loss Account) of AGRODRON LEVANTE S.L. for the period ending 31 December 2018 (31/12/2018), and deduce the exact date in 2017 on which the fleet of agricultural drones was acquired.
  2. Construct and justify the balance sheet at 24:00 on 31 December 2018 (31/12/2018), detailing all intermediate cash and accrual calculations.
  3. Determine the values of the ROA and ROE ratios in 2018.
  4. Indicate which items of the balance sheet at 31 December 2018 (31/12/2018) would be affected and the exact amount of the effect if the decision was made before the end of 2018 to distribute the same dividend, but to pay it on 30 June 2019 (30/06/2019), and assuming simultaneously that the company had decided not to offset the loss of 2017 before calculating the 30% dividend payout.

The external auditor of TALLERES AERONÁUTICOS DEL HENARES S.A. (TAHSA), a company of Alcalá de Henares dedicated to the machining of titanium brackets and fittings for the aircraft structures industry, must issue the audit report on the financial statements (balance sheet and Income Statement) as of 31 December 2019 (31/12/2019). The auditor has the balance of the company as of 31 December 2018 (31/12/2018), which is included below, and the following operations that have taken place during the period from 1 January 2019 (01/01/2019) to 31 December 2019 (31/12/2019).

I. The company has sold during the year 2.400 brackets at a price of 8 m.u. / unit (every month the same amount, 200 u.). A part of the sales of each month, always the same percentage, is charged in cash in the moment of the sale; the rest is payable to 90 days. Unfortunately the commercial department has lost the contract that fixes this percentage.

II. During the first quarter of 2019, the unpaid taxes and the outstanding supplier balances of the previous year were paid. The customer debt outstanding from the previous year was charged in January, except 160 m.u. from an airline component maker declared in insolvency on 1 March 2019 (01/03/2019), which is definitively lost.

III. At 31 December 2018 (31/12/2018) there is a stock (stock in stock) of 800 kg of titanium bar valued at 1,50 m.u. / kg. On 1 February 2019 (01/02/2019) the company purchased 3.000 kg at 1,50 m.u. / kg, 50% payable to 60 days and the other 50% deferred until 1 February 2020 (01/02/2020). On 1 August 2019 (01/08/2019) it purchased 2.000 kg more at the same price, payable to 120 days. The count of 31 December 2019 (31/12/2019) shows 900 kg in the warehouse.

IV. Personnel expenses have been 400 m.u. / month (to which 120 m.u. / month must be added for Social Security); salaries are paid in the month in which they are produced and Social Security the month after. General expenses (electricity, insurance, cleaning) amount to 150 m.u. / month and are paid two months after being made.

V. The machinery of the balance of 2018 was bought on 1 January 2016 (01/01/2016) and is amortized linearly in 10 years with residual value zero. On 1 April 2019 (01/04/2019) the company bought a 5-axis CNC centre that cost 4.800 m.u., paid in full in cash that day. To finance it, the same day a bank granted a loan of 3.600 m.u. at 5% annual interest, to be returned in one single payment on 1 April 2022 (01/04/2022); the interest is paid every 1 April for the year that ends that day. The CNC centre will be amortized linearly in 8 years with a residual value of 480 m.u.

VI. The long-term loan of the balance of 2018 bears 4% annual interest. The company returns 300 m.u. of principal every 30 June and every 31 December, paying the same days the interest of the semester calculated on the debt at the beginning of the semester.

VII. On 1 October 2019 (01/10/2019) the shareholders subscribed a capital increase of 500 new shares of 2 m.u. nominal value, without issue premium, disbursing that day only 50%; the rest will be called in 2020. On 15 November 2019 (15/11/2019) the company received in cash a dividend of 80 m.u. from its financial shares in AEROPIEZAS S.A., a permanent investment.

items.statement_html:
AVIÓNICA DEL EBRO S.L. (AVIEBRO), a Zaragoza workshop dedicated to the repair and calibration of avionics equipment for regional airlines and flying schools, must present to the bank that finances it the financial statements (balance sheet and Income Statement) as of 30 June 2020 (30/06/2020). The financial director has the balance of 31 December 2019 (31/12/2019), included below, and the following operations of the first semester, from 1 January 2020 (01/01/2020) to 30 June 2020 (30/06/2020):

I. The company has invoiced repairs for 1.600 m.u. every month. The payment condition agreed with the customers is payable to 60 days. A regional airline, which represents 40% of the invoicing of every month, surpassed in March the annual volume agreed in its contract, and from 1 April 2020 (01/04/2020) it receives a discount of 5% on all its invoices.

II. The customer debt outstanding at 31 December 2019 (31/12/2019) was charged in January, except 250 m.u. from a flying school that has been granted to pay it on 30 September 2020 (30/09/2020). The suppliers of the previous year were paid in February. As the company closed 2019 with losses, there were no taxes to pay.

III. At 31 December 2019 (31/12/2019) there is a stock (stock in stock) of 300 spare parts valued at 2 m.u. / unit. On 1 February 2020 (01/02/2020) the company purchased 400 parts at 2 m.u., 50% paid in cash and 50% payable to 90 days; on 1 May 2020 (01/05/2020) it purchased 300 parts more at the same price, payable to 120 days. At 30 June 2020 (30/06/2020) there remain 250 parts in the warehouse.

IV. The technicians cost 600 m.u. / month, paid in the same month, to which 180 m.u. / month of Social Security must be added, paid the month after. The overheads (electricity, telephone, cleaning) are 100 m.u. / month and are paid two months after being made. On 1 March 2020 (01/03/2020) the company carried out a renting contract for a test bench of 120 m.u. monthly, paid at the end of each month.

V. The patent of the balance (a calibration procedure) is amortized linearly in 5 years with residual value zero; the computer equipment was bought on 1 January 2019 (01/01/2019) and is amortized linearly in 3 years with residual value zero.

VI. On 1 April 2020 (01/04/2020) AVIEBRO bought a small hangar next to the airport: the building is valued at 2.000 m.u. and the land at 1.000 m.u. It paid 20% in cash and the rest with a mortgage loan at 4% annual interest, to be returned in installments of 120 m.u. every 1 October and every 1 April, the first one on 1 October 2020 (01/10/2020); the same days it pays the interest of the semester calculated on the debt at the beginning of the semester. The building is amortized linearly in 50 years with residual value zero.

VII. The long-term loan of the balance bears 5% annual interest, which is paid every 31 December, and it is returned in one single payment on 31 December 2022 (31/12/2022).

VIII. The corporation tax is 25%. The taxable base of the semester is the profit before taxes minus the losses from previous years still pending to offset, and the resulting tax will be paid on 20 July 2020 (20/07/2020) (counted in the balance as "taxes to pay"). No dividends are distributed at the half-year.

Time window: six months, 01/01/2020–30/06/2020. Depreciation and interest are prorated by months; expenses are recorded when incurred even if they are paid later [Slide 8].

Hypotheses:

  1. The airline's discount applies to the invoices of April, May and June only.
  2. "Payable to 90 days" from 1 February means payment on 1 May; "payable to 120 days" from 1 May means payment at the end of August, outside the semester.
  3. The losses from previous years are offset for tax purposes, but they stay in the balance sheet until the annual meeting distributes the profit of the year; the result of the semester is shown separately in equity.
  4. Land is not depreciated.

Extension (not defined in the course decks). $\text{ROA} = \text{Income from operations}/\text{Total assets}$ and $\text{ROE} = \text{Net profit}/\text{Owners equity}$, both for the semester and on the balance at 30/06/2020.

The chief financial officer (CFO) of COMPOSITES AEROESPACIALES DE ÁLAVA S.A. (CAESA), a company of Vitoria dedicated to the manufacturing of carbon-fibre fairings for helicopters, is closing the books of the year 2021. The balance of the company at 31 December 2020 (31/12/2020) is included below; the operations of the period from 1 January 2021 (01/01/2021) to 31 December 2021 (31/12/2021) have been the following:

I. The company has sold 1.200 fairings at a price of 30 m.u. / unit (every month the same amount, 100 u.). Of the sales of every month, 20% is charged in cash and the remaining 80% is payable to 60 days. The customer debt of the previous year was charged in January, and the suppliers and the unpaid taxes of the previous year were paid in January and in April respectively.

II. At 31 December 2020 (31/12/2020) there is a stock (stock in stock) of 500 kg of epoxy resin valued at 3 m.u. / kg. On 1 March 2021 (01/03/2021) the company purchased 4.000 kg at 3 m.u. / kg, paying 30% in cash and the remaining 70% in two equal parts, on 1 September 2021 (01/09/2021) and on 1 March 2022 (01/03/2022). At 31 December 2021 (31/12/2021) there remain 700 kg in the warehouse.

III. The fixed salaries are 1.000 m.u. / month, paid in the same month, to which 300 m.u. / month of Social Security must be added, paid the month after. Variable wages of the lamination staff amounted in 2021 to 1.200 m.u. (paid in cash). The external supplies (energy for the autoclaves) are 250 m.u. / month and are paid two months after being made.

IV. The autoclave of the balance was bought on 1 January 2018 (01/01/2018) and is amortized linearly in 10 years with a residual value of 1.000 m.u. On 1 July 2021 (01/07/2021) CAESA put into service a second autoclave of 6.000 m.u. (amortized linearly in 10 years with a residual value of 600 m.u.) together with a software license for the control of the curing cycles of 1.200 m.u. (amortized linearly in 3 years with residual value zero), both paid in full in cash that day.

V. items.statement_html:
HELIPUERTOS Y SERVICIOS DEL CANTÁBRICO S.L. (HESECA) operates one helicopter from Santander for charter flights, offshore inspections and maintenance of other operators' aircraft. A trainee of the accounting firm that keeps its books has prepared, instead of the financial statements, the following summary of the ledger accounts of 2022, from 1 January 2022 (01/01/2022) to 31 December 2022 (31/12/2022). The partner of the firm asks you to prepare the balance sheet and the Income Statement as of 31 December 2022 (31/12/2022).

Opening balances at 1 January 2022 (01/01/2022): Customers 3.000; Spare parts 1.000; Bank 2.000; Helicopter (cost) 24.000; Accumulated depreciation of the helicopter 4.500; Van (cost) 1.800; Accumulated depreciation of the van 300; Paid-in capital 18.000; Reserves 1.500; Suppliers 1.200; Unpaid taxes 800; Bank loan 5.500.

Customers account: opening balance 3.000; invoiced in 2022 for flights and maintenance 34.000; collected in 2022 31.000; on 1 September 2022 (01/09/2022) a balance of 400 m.u. from an operator declared in bankruptcy was written off as definitively unrecoverable.

Spare parts and suppliers accounts: on 1 March 2022 (01/03/2022) parts were purchased for 3.000 m.u., 50% paid in cash and the rest payable to 60 days; on 1 September 2022 (01/09/2022) parts were purchased for 3.000 m.u. more, 50% payable to 30 days and the other 50% deferred until 1 March 2023 (01/03/2023). The suppliers' balance of the previous year was paid in January. The physical count of 31 December 2022 (31/12/2022) values the stock (stock in stock) of parts at 1.400 m.u.

Expense accounts (all paid by bank unless indicated): fuel 4.800; salaries of pilots and mechanics 9.600; Social Security 3.000, of which the contribution of December (250) is paid in January 2023; hangar rent 200 m.u. / month; on 1 October 2022 (01/10/2022) the annual insurance premium of the helicopter, 1.200 m.u., covering from 1 October 2022 (01/10/2022) to 30 September 2023 (30/09/2023), was paid in full. The unpaid taxes of 2021 were paid in January.

Fixed assets: the helicopter is amortized linearly in 12 years with a residual value of 10% of its cost, and was bought on a date that the trainee could not find; the van was bought on 1 January 2021 (01/01/2021) and is amortized linearly in 6 years with residual value zero.

Financing: the bank loan was granted on 1 January 2020 (01/01/2020) for 7.500 m.u. at 6% annual interest; every 31 December the company returns 1.000 m.u. and pays the interest calculated on the debt at the beginning of the year. On 1 May 2022 (01/05/2022) a bank opened a credit line with a limit of 4.000 m.u.: HESECA drew 2.000 m.u. that day and 1.000 m.u. more on 1 September 2022 (01/09/2022); it pays 9% annual interest only on the amount drawn, every 31 July, 31 October and 31 January, for the three months then ended.

Closing: the results are declared at 23:59 hrs on 31 December 2022 (31/12/2022). The corporation tax is 30% and will be paid in July 2023 ("taxes to pay"). The partners decided on 31 December 2022 (31/12/2022) a dividend of 30% of the profit after taxes, to be paid on 15 March 2023 (15/03/2023); the rest goes to reserves.

Required:

  1. Deduce the exact date on which the helicopter was purchased, and construct the Income Statement (Profit and Loss Account) of HESECA for the year 2022.
  2. Calculate the bank balance at 31 December 2022 (31/12/2022) and construct the balance sheet at that date, justifying the classification of every item.
  3. Determine the values of the ROA and ROE ratios in 2022, and indicate the effect on the balance sheet if the dividend had been paid at 24:00 on 31 December 2022 (31/12/2022).
  4. The trainee had recorded the whole insurance premium of 1.200 m.u. as an expense of 2022. Indicate what changes this error would produce in the Income Statement, the distribution of the profit and the balance sheet, and explain which statement it distorts and why.
